content: To vote in India, you must be a registered voter. Registration is done through the Election Commission of India (ECI) via the National Voters' Service Portal (NVSP) or the Voter Helpline App.
steps: Visit the NVSP portal or download the Voter Helpline App.
Fill out Form 6 for fresh registration.
Upload required documents: Proof of age (Birth Certificate/Aadhaar) and Proof of residence.
Submit the application. A Booth Level Officer (BLO) will visit for verification.
Once verified, your EPIC card will be generated and sent via post.
examples: Rahul just turned 18. He goes to nvsp.in, fills Form 6 with his Aadhaar and photo, and receives his Voter ID in 4 weeks.

content: On election day, you must go to your assigned polling booth. The process involves verification, marking with indelible ink, and casting your vote on the EVM.
steps: Check your name in the electoral roll and find your polling booth.
Carry your EPIC card or an alternative ID (like Aadhaar/DL).
The first polling official checks your name and ID.
The second official inks your finger and gives you a slip.
The third official takes the slip and enables the EVM.
Go to the voting compartment, press the button next to your candidate's symbol on the EVM.
Check the VVPAT window for a 7-second slip confirmation of your vote.
examples: Priya visits the local school (polling booth), shows her Aadhaar, gets the blue ink mark, and presses the EVM button for her chosen party.

content: Every voter has the right to a free and fair election. You have the right to secrecy and the right to report any misconduct.
steps: Vote without fear or influence from anyone.
Maintain the secrecy of your vote.
Use NOTA (None Of The Above) if you don't support any candidate.
Report bribery or misconduct to the Election Observer or via C-Vigil app.
examples: If someone tries to offer money for a vote, Suresh uses the C-Vigil app to report it anonymously to the ECI.

content: After polling ends, EVMs are sealed and stored in strong rooms. On the counting day, they are opened in the presence of candidates and observers.
steps: EVMs are transported to counting centers under tight security.
Votes are counted round by round for each constituency.
VVPAT slips are verified for a few randomly selected booths.
The candidate with the most votes is declared the winner.
The Election Commission officially notifies the results.
examples: On counting day, news channels show the 'lead' as EVM totals are tallied, and finally, the Returning Officer issues a certificate to the winner.
